title: 255. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Comparing Slopes of Linear Functions
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify which linear function has the greater slope by comparing coefficients of \(x\).
questions.question: Which linear function has the greater slope?
questions.explanation: In the form \(y=mx+b\), the slope is the coefficient of \(x\). For \(y=3x+1\), the slope is \(3\). For \(y=2x+5\), the slope is \(2\). Since \(3>2\), the function \(y=3x+1\) has the greater slope. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the coefficients of \(x\) in the two equations.

questions.concept: Comparing a Slope with a Threshold
questions.learningObjective: Determine which linear function has a slope greater than \(1\).
questions.question: Which function has a slope greater than \(1\)?
questions.explanation: The slope of \(y=2x+1\) is \(2\), and \(2>1\). The slope of \(y=0.5x+3\) is \(0.5\), and \(0.5<1\). Therefore only \(y=2x+1\) has a slope greater than \(1\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Compare each coefficient of \(x\) with the number \(1\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify the linear function with a decreasing graph by comparing slope signs.
questions.question: Which linear function is decreasing?
questions.explanation: A linear function is decreasing when its slope is negative. For \(y=3x+2\), the slope is \(3>0\), so the graph increases. For \(y=-2x+1\), the slope is \(-2<0\), so the graph decreases. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether the coefficient of \(x\) is positive or negative.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which line is steeper by comparing absolute values of slopes.
questions.question: Which line is steeper?
questions.explanation: Steepness is determined by the absolute value of the slope. For \(y=2x+1\), \(|2|=2\). For \(y=-4x+3\), \(|-4|=4\). Since \(4>2\), the line \(y=-4x+3\) is steeper. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the absolute values of the slopes, not their signs.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a line parallel to a given line by comparing slopes.
questions.question: Which line is parallel to \(y=3x-4\)?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have the same slope. The line \(y=3x-4\) has slope \(3\). The line \(y=3x+7\) also has slope \(3\), so it is parallel to the given line. The line \(y=-3x+2\) has slope \(-3\), so it is not parallel. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: Parallel lines must have equal slopes.

questions.concept: Perpendicular Lines and Negative Reciprocal Slopes
questions.learningObjective: Identify a line perpendicular to a given line by comparing slopes.
questions.question: Which line is perpendicular to \(y=2x+1\)?
questions.explanation: Two lines are perpendicular when their slopes are negative reciprocals. The slope of \(y=2x+1\) is \(2\). The negative reciprocal of \(2\) is \(-\frac{1}{2}\). The line \(y=-\frac{1}{2}x+5\) has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\), so it is perpendicular to the given line. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Multiply the two slopes; perpendicular slopes have a product of \(-1\).

questions.learningObjective: Compare slopes of two lines by calculating each slope from two points.
questions.question: Line \(L_1\) passes through \((0,0)\) and \((1,2)\). Line \(L_2\) passes through \((0,0)\) and \((1,3)\). Which line has the greater slope?
questions.explanation: For \(L_1\), the slope is \(\frac{2-0}{1-0}=2\). For \(L_2\), the slope is \(\frac{3-0}{1-0}=3\). Since \(3>2\), line \(L_2\) has the greater slope. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Use the slope formula \(m=\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\) for each line.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which line has the more negative slope by comparing slope values.
questions.question: Which line has the smaller, more negative slope?
questions.explanation: For \(y=-2x+5\), the slope is \(-2\). For \(y=-5x+1\), the slope is \(-5\). On the number line, \(-5<-2\), so \(-5\) is the smaller, more negative slope. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the two negative numbers on the number line.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which table represents a line with the greater slope.
questions.question: Table A shows \(x:0,1,2\) and \(y:1,3,5\). Table B shows \(x:0,1,2\) and \(y:1,4,7\). Which table represents the line with the greater slope?
questions.explanation: For Table A, as \(x\) increases by \(1\), \(y\) increases by \(2\), so the slope is \(2\). For Table B, as \(x\) increases by \(1\), \(y\) increases by \(3\), so the slope is \(3\). Since \(3>2\), Table B represents the line with the greater slope. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Compare the change in \(y\) for each unit increase in \(x\).

questions.learningObjective: Compare the slopes of a line given by two points and a line given by an equation.
questions.question: Line \(L_1\) passes through \((1,1)\) and \((3,5)\). Line \(L_2\) is \(y=3x-2\). Which line has the greater slope?
questions.explanation: For \(L_1\), the slope is \(\frac{5-1}{3-1}=\frac{4}{2}=2\). For \(L_2\), the slope is the coefficient of \(x\), which is \(3\). Since \(3>2\), line \(L_2\) has the greater slope. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Calculate the slope of \(L_1\) from the two points, then compare it with the slope of \(L_2\).
